Chemists change molecules with named edits (put a fluorine on an aromatic carbon, turn a CH into N, remove a substituent ...) and compute exact properties. Biologists run assays: the activity against the target and toxicity, both hidden functions of the structure, measured with noise and expensive. Only molecules someone has made (the starting ones and the products of edits) can be assayed, so the two roles depend on each other.

Tasks climb a ladder (a hit, then a lead, then a candidate with low toxicity); thresholds are calibrated at reset by a search over the edit space, so every episode is solvable.
